Supersymmetry (SUSY)

 Home Physics Branches of physics
OurBigBook.com Words: 11k Articles: 248
Supersymmetry extends spacetime symmetry by odd supercharges that interchange boson and fermion states. Their Super-Poincaré algebra pairs positive-energy states into supermultiplets and gives energy positivity in global supersymmetry. Superspace and superfields package the component fields into representations of this symmetry.

Supersymmetric action (S=∫d4x[∫d4θK+∫d2θW+h.c.])

Words: 401 Articles: 6
Supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
A supersymmetric action is invariant under supersymmetry up to boundary terms. For ordinary four-dimensional chiral superfields, a full superspace integration of a real Kähler potential and a chiral superspace integration of a superpotential provide the two-derivative ungauged action.

Two-derivative global supersymmetric gauge action (∫d4θK+∫d2θ[W+41​fab​WaαWαb​]+h.c.)

Words: 60
Supersymmetric action OurBigBook.com
A two-derivative four-dimensional N=1 gauge action is specified by a real gauge-invariant Kähler potential, a gauge-invariant holomorphic superpotential, and a holomorphic symmetric gauge kinetic function. A constant Fayet–Iliopoulos term is additionally allowed for an Abelian gauge factor. Renormalizability restricts the matter kinetic function to a quadratic form, the superpotential to degree at most three, and the gauge kinetic function to a constant invariant tensor.

Gauge kinetic function (41​∫d2θfab​(Φ)WaαWαb​+h.c.)

Words: 110 Articles: 1
Supersymmetric action OurBigBook.com
The gauge kinetic function is a symmetric holomorphic function of chiral superfields multiplying the gauge field-strength F-term. Its real part controls gauge kinetic coefficients and its imaginary part controls topological-angle terms. Its Wilsonian perturbative correction is constrained by one-loop exactness of the holomorphic gauge kinetic function; canonical and one-particle-irreducible gauge couplings require separate normalization and infrared analysis.
// Target: supersymmetry.bigb

Holomorphic gauge coupling (f=gh−2​−iϑ/(8π2))

Words: 61
Gauge kinetic function OurBigBook.com
A holomorphic gauge coupling is the coefficient of the gauge kinetic F-term in a local Wilsonian effective action written in holomorphic variables. In a common normalization its real part is 1/gh2​. The continuous perturbative shift of its topological angle, together with holomorphy, restricts its beta function to one-loop order. Wave-function renormalization and anomalous canonical field rescalings distinguish it from the physical gauge coupling.
// Target: supersymmetry.bigb

Grassmann-valued classical supersymmetric mechanics

Words: 169 Articles: 1
Supersymmetric action OurBigBook.com
A classical supersymmetric mechanical model takes its coordinates in a Grassmann algebra: the position is even and the fermionic coordinates are odd. Time differentiation is even, while variation with respect to an odd coordinate uses Grassmann derivatives. For example, moving an odd variation to the left and integrating by parts gives δ∫ψψ˙​dt=2∫δψψ˙​dt.
For the real variant L=x˙2/2+U2/2−ψ1​ψ˙​1​/2+ψ2​ψ˙​2​/2+U′ψ1​ψ2​, the Euler-Lagrange equations are
x¨=UU′+U′′ψ1​ψ2​,ψ˙​1​=U′ψ2​,ψ˙​2​=U′ψ1​.
(1)
The conserved even energy is E=x˙2/2−U2/2−U′ψ1​ψ2​ and the odd supercharges are Q1​=x˙ψ1​−Uψ2​, Q2​=x˙ψ2​−Uψ1​. For example, Q˙​i​=U′′ψ1​ψ2​ψi​=0, since each odd element squares to zero. Also d(ψ1​ψ2​)/dt=U′(ψ22​+ψ12​)=0, which proves E˙=0.

First-order zero-energy solution in Grassmann supersymmetric mechanics

Words: 68
Grassmann-valued classical supersymmetric mechanics OurBigBook.com
In the real Grassmann-valued classical supersymmetric mechanics variant, impose x˙=U(x) and ψ2​=−ψ1​. Then ψ1​ψ2​=0, and differentiating the first-order equation gives x¨=UU′. The remaining Euler-Lagrange equations reduce to ψ˙​1​=−U′ψ1​. These solutions have E=0 but Q1​=2Uψ1​=−Q2​, which need not vanish: d(Uψ1​)/dt=U′Uψ1​−UU′ψ1​=0.
For U=1+cx, one obtains x(t)=ectx0​+(ect−1)/c and ψ1​(t)=e−ctψ10​ when c=0. At c=0, the limiting solution is x(t)=x0​+t, ψ1​(t)=ψ10​. In either case Q1​=2(1+cx0​)ψ10​.

Renormalizable chiral-superfield action

Words: 33
Supersymmetric action OurBigBook.com
In four spacetime dimensions, power-counting renormalizability restricts an ungauged chiral action to a canonical quadratic Kähler potential, up to transformations, and a superpotential of degree at most three. Terms of larger degree belong to an effective field theory.

Worldline supersymmetry algebra ({Q,Q}D​=−2iH)

Words: 36
Supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
The spinning particle constraints Q=ψmpm​ and H=p2/2 obey {Q,Q}D​=−2iH and {Q,H}D​=0. In the quantum theory Q​2=H, so the fermionic physical-state equation implies the mass-shell equation.

Supersymmetric localization

Words: 70 Articles: 1
Supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
A symmetry-preserving deformation can leave protected observables unchanged while concentrating their integral on a smaller critical locus. Supersymmetric Ward identities justify the deformation; convergence and boundary terms must be controlled.

Localization of a zero-dimensional polynomial model (⟨f⟩=π∑a​ma​f(za​))

Words: 43
Supersymmetric localization OurBigBook.com
With P=W′ a nonconstant polynomial, positive area measure and Berezin integration oriented positively, a holomorphic polynomial insertion in S=∣P∣2−P′θ1​θ2​−P′θˉ1​θˉ2​ equals π∑a​ma​f(za​), where P(za​)=0 and ma​ is the multiplicity of a root. Rescaling P by t>0 leaves the insertion fixed and localizes it as t→∞.

Supersymmetric Ward identity (⟨QX⟩=0)

Words: 30
Supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
If an odd graded derivation Q preserves the action and integration measure, then ⟨QX⟩=0 whenever boundary contributions and anomalies vanish. This applies to finite-dimensional zero-dimensional supersymmetric field theories as well as suitably regulated field integrals.

Zero-dimensional supersymmetric field theory

Words: 54 Articles: 1
Supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
A zero-dimensional model is a finite-dimensional integral with bosonic and Grassmann variables, rather than a field depending on spacetime. Odd graded derivations preserve its action and integration measure. Such models expose supersymmetric Ward identities and supersymmetric localization without spacetime dynamics.

Odd symmetries of a zero-dimensional polynomial model (V1​=θ1​∂z​−Pˉ∂θ2​​)

Words: 22
Zero-dimensional supersymmetric field theory OurBigBook.com
For P=W′ and S=∣P∣2−P′θ1​θ2​−P′θˉ1​θˉ2​, four odd graded derivations preserve S: θ1​∂z​−Pˉ∂θ2​​, θ2​∂z​+Pˉ∂θ1​​ and their barred counterparts. Left Grassmann derivatives fix the signs.

Extended supersymmetry (N>1)

Words: 105 Articles: 2
Supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
In four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, extended supersymmetry has more than one independent Weyl spinor supercharge, together with their adjoints. The index A=1,…,N distinguishes these supercharges.

Chirality constraint on extended supersymmetry

Words: 57
Extended supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
In a four-dimensional theory with unbroken N≥2 supersymmetry, a full charged hypermultiplet contains N=1 chiral superfields in R and R. Their net complex chiral gauge spectrum vanishes. The vector multiplet is in the real adjoint gauge group representation. Half-hypermultiplets in pseudoreal representations do not supply genuinely complex gauge chirality. Thus the chiral matter of the Standard Model can have at most unbroken N=1 supersymmetry in four dimensions.

Hypermultiplet

Words: 27
Extended supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
A full four-dimensional N=2 hypermultiplet is a matter supermultiplet equivalent to two N=1 chiral superfields in conjugate gauge group representations. Pseudoreal representations can admit half-hypermultiplets; these do not provide genuinely complex chiral gauge spectra.

Two-dimensional N=(2,2) supersymmetry (2D N=(2,2) SUSY)

Words: 75 Articles: 2
Supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
Two-dimensional N=(2,2) supersymmetry has independent left- and right-moving complex supercharges. Its superspace uses θ±,θˉ± and supports both chiral and twisted chiral superfields.

Twisted chiral superfield

Words: 52 Articles: 1
Two-dimensional N=(2,2) supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
A twisted chiral superfield obeys Dˉ+​Σ=D−​Σ=0. In an Abelian gauge theory the field-strength multiplet Σ=Dˉ+​D−​V is gauge invariant and twisted chiral.

Twisted superpotential (W)

Words: 28
Twisted chiral superfield OurBigBook.com
A twisted superpotential is a holomorphic function of twisted chiral superfields integrated over dθ+dθˉ− superspace. Its highest component varies by a spacetime total derivative under two-dimensional N=(2,2) supersymmetry.

Two-dimensional N=(0,2) supersymmetry (2D N=(0,2) SUSY)

Words: 51 Articles: 1
Supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
Two-dimensional N=(0,2) supersymmetry retains one complex right-moving supercharge. Its basic matter multiplets are chiral superfields containing a scalar and right-moving fermion, and Fermi superfields containing a left-moving fermion and an auxiliary scalar.

Fermi superfield

Words: 18
Two-dimensional N=(0,2) supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
A Fermi superfield Λ−a​ obeys Dˉ+​Λ−a​=fa​(Φ). A supersymmetric J-type coupling ∫dθ+Λ−a​Ja(Φ) requires ∑a​fa​Ja=0.

Four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetry (4D N=1 SUSY)

Words: 5k Articles: 111
Supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
Four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetry has one Weyl-spinor supercharge and four real supercharges.

Super-Poincaré group

Words: 45
Four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
The Super-Poincaré group combines Lorentz transformations and supertranslations. Its even part acts by spin-group transformations and ordinary spacetime translations; odd parameters generate the supercharges. Their graded commutator closes on translations through the Super-Poincaré algebra. A superspace tensor built from invariant coframes and Lorentz-invariant contractions is invariant under the full group.

Supercurrent (Sαμ​)

Words: 34
Four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
The supercurrent is the spinor-valued Noether current of rigid supersymmetry. Its spatial integral is a supercharge. Localizing the supersymmetry parameter produces ∂μ​ϵˉSμ in the variation of the action; a gravitino coupling cancels this term and starts the Noether gauging procedure.

Super-Poincaré algebra

Words: 810 Articles: 16
Four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetry OurBigBook.com
The super-Poincaré algebra extends the Poincare algebra by odd spinor generators. In four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetry, {Qα​,Qˉ​β˙​​}=2σαβ˙​μ​Pμ​ and the equal-chirality anticommutators vanish.

Domain-wall charge in N=1 supersymmetry (TBPS​=2∣ΔW∣)

Words: 62
Super-Poincaré algebra OurBigBook.com
A supersymmetric domain wall contributes a boundary or tensorial charge to the extended anticommutator of supercharges. It is not the Lorentz-scalar central charge of an extended particle algebra. The wall's energy per unit area can cancel this charge in half the real charge combinations, giving the BPS tension bound and half-supersymmetry preservation. This does not contradict the rank classification for the ordinary algebra without wall charges.

Supertranslation

Words: 34
Super-Poincaré algebra OurBigBook.com
A supertranslation is generated by translations and supercharges, excluding the Lorentz transformations. For flat Majorana superspace with Πm=dXm+iθˉγmdθ, the rigid odd transformation δθ=ϵ, δXm=−iϵˉγmθ leaves Πm invariant. Its commutator gives an ordinary translation.

Superspace differential realization of N=1 supercharges ({Qα​,Qˉ​β˙​​}=2σαβ˙​μ​Pμ​)

Words: 73
Super-Poincaré algebra OurBigBook.com
With left Grassmann derivatives, define Pμ​=−i∂μ​, Qα​=−i∂θα​−σαγ˙​μ​θˉγ˙​∂μ​ and Qˉ​β˙​​=i∂θˉβ˙​​+θγσγβ˙​μ​∂μ​. The anticommutators of the derivative parts and of the coordinate parts vanish. Each mixed derivative/coordinate pair contributes −iσμ∂μ​ by the graded product rule, giving the displayed mixed anticommutator. Equal-chirality anticommutators vanish, and all these operators commute with translations. Under Lorentz transformations their spinor indices transform in conjugate Weyl spinor representations, completing the minimal Super-Poincaré algebra. A convention for left derivatives is essential to the signs.

Supercharges commute with translations ([Pμ,Qα​]=0)

Words: 27
Super-Poincaré algebra OurBigBook.com
In the minimal Super-Poincaré algebra, Lorentz covariance allows [Pμ,Qα​]=Aσαβ˙​μ​Qˉ​β˙​. The graded Jacobi identity with Pμ,Qα​,Qβ​ forces A=0. Thus each supercharge preserves four-momentum and its mass Casimir, giving supersymmetric mass degeneracy in an unbroken physical supermultiplet.

If null, the stabilizer of a parallel spinor in Spin(1,3) contains only null rotations, and the local vacuum metric is ds2=−2dudv+dx2+dy2+H(u,x,y)du2 with Hxx​+Hyy​=0. Constant spinors obeying γ+ϵ=0 are parallel. These are local statements; global quotients must preserve a compatible spin structure.

Minimal four-dimensional supergravity (N=1,(eμ​a,ψμ​))

Words: 305 Articles: 5
Supergravity OurBigBook.com
Minimal four-dimensional supergravity couples a graviton to one Majorana gravitino. In the normalization δeμ​a=2κϵˉγaψμ​, δψμ​=∇μ​ϵ/κ, its action through quadratic fermion order is ∫e[R/(2κ2)−2ψˉ​μ​γμνρ∇ν​ψρ​]. Rescaling the gravitino and parameter by two gives the usual canonical kinetic coefficient −1/2. The curvature identity γμνρ∇ν​∇ρ​ϵ=Gμνγν​ϵ/2 cancels the Einstein-Hilbert variation against the Rarita-Schwinger variation. The omitted cubic-fermion variations require the quartic-fermion completion.

Old-minimal supergravity ((eμ​a,ψμ​,M,bμ​))

Words: 41
Minimal four-dimensional supergravity OurBigBook.com
Old-minimal four-dimensional supergravity adds a complex scalar M and a real vector bμ​ to the vierbein and gravitino. These six real bosonic auxiliary field components have no propagating kinetic terms. They balance the off-shell component count of minimal supergravity and permit the local supersymmetry algebra to close without imposing the propagating Euler-Lagrange field equations.

Off-shell component count of minimal supergravity (6 bosonic+12 fermionic components)

Words: 53
Minimal four-dimensional supergravity OurBigBook.com
A four-dimensional Majorana spinor gravitino has 4×4=16 real components, minus four local supersymmetry gauge functions, leaving twelve before using any Euler-Lagrange field equation. A vierbein has sixteen real components, minus six local Lorentz transformation and four diffeomorphism gauge functions, leaving six. Equivalently, a symmetric metric tensor has 10−4=6. The propagating graviton and massless gravitino each have two states on shell. Six bosonic auxiliary field components complete an off-shell supergravity multiplet.

Gravitino-induced torsion (Tμν​a=2κ2​ψˉ​μ​γaψν​)

Words: 45
Minimal four-dimensional supergravity OurBigBook.com
With canonical Rarita-Schwinger field normalization, one convention gives the displayed torsion tensor. Its contorsion tensor is Kμab​=κ2(ψˉ​μ​γa​ψb​−ψˉ​μ​γb​ψa​+ψˉ​a​γμ​ψb​)/4. The algebraic spin connection equation determines ω=ω(e)+K; substituting it in the action produces four-fermion terms. This is an instance of Einstein-Cartan theory and is efficiently varied using the 1.5-order formalism. A rescaled gravitino changes the displayed coefficient.

Supergravity coupling of an Abelian vector multiplet ((Aμ​,λ))

Words: 65
Minimal four-dimensional supergravity OurBigBook.com
An Abelian vector multiplet contains a Maxwell field and a Majorana gaugino. With the doubled gravitino normalization, add e[−F2/4−λˉ∇λ/2−(κ/2)ψˉ​μ​Fab​γabγμλ]. The leading transformations are δAμ​=ϵˉγμ​λ and δλ=−Fab​γabϵ/2. Promoting the rigid parameter to a function produces the current (Fab​/2)γabγμλ multiplying ∇μ​ϵˉ; the gravitino-current term cancels it. The Clifford identity (Fab​γab)γμ(Fcd​γcd)=8TEMμν​γν​ cancels the Maxwell stress variation. Supercovariant field strengths and quartic fermions complete the transformations beyond this order.

Anti-de Sitter deformation of minimal supergravity (Λ=−3m2,Dμ​=∇μ​+(m/2)γμ​)

Words: 43
Minimal four-dimensional supergravity OurBigBook.com
A real cosmological deformation adds 3m2e/κ2+2meψˉ​μ​γμνψν​ and changes the gravitino variation to Dμ​ϵ/κ. The modified commutator identity is γμνρDν​Dρ​ϵ=(Gμν+Λgμν)γν​ϵ/2. It fixes the negative cosmological constant in terms of the gravitino mass parameter. A positive cosmological constant is not obtained by this real unbroken minimal deformation.

Maximal nine-dimensional supergravity (N=2,32 real supercharges)

Words: 55
Supergravity OurBigBook.com
The ungauged maximal nine-dimensional supergravity zero-mode multiplet has one metric, three vectors, two two-forms, one three-form and three scalars, giving 128 bosonic states. Two Majorana gravitini and four Majorana spin-one-half fields give 128 fermionic states. Flat-circle reductions of massless type IIA and type IIB theories, and a flat-two-torus reduction of eleven-dimensional supergravity, give this same nonchiral spectrum.

Type IIB supergravity

Words: 36
Supergravity OurBigBook.com
Type IIB supergravity is the chiral ten-dimensional maximal supergravity with metric, Kalb–Ramond field, dilaton, Ramond-Ramond zero-form, two-form and four-form potentials, and a self-dual five-form field strength. Two same-chirality Majorana-Weyl gravitini and two opposite-to-gravitino-chirality Majorana-Weyl dilatini complete its 128+128 massless spectrum.

Type IIA supergravity

Words: 68 Articles: 2
Supergravity OurBigBook.com
Massless type IIA supergravity is the nonchiral ten-dimensional maximal supergravity with metric, Kalb–Ramond field, dilaton, Ramond-Ramond one-form and three-form potentials, two opposite-chirality Majorana-Weyl gravitini, and two opposite-chirality Majorana-Weyl dilatini. Its massless spectrum has 128 bosonic and 128 fermionic polarizations. The two supercharges have opposite ten-dimensional chirality.

Massive type IIA supergravity

Words: 25 Articles: 1
Type IIA supergravity OurBigBook.com
Romans mass (F0​=m)
Words: 25
Massive type IIA supergravity OurBigBook.com
The zero-form field strength deforms massless type IIA supergravity. A D8-brane changes this flux across its worldvolume; it is therefore outside the elementary massless M-theory circle duality dictionary.

Dilatino (λ)

Words: 37
Supergravity OurBigBook.com
A dilatino is a spin-one-half fermionic partner in a supergravity theory containing a dilaton. Type IIA and type IIB theories each contain two Majorana-Weyl dilatini with eight physical polarizations apiece. Their chirality assignments differ between the two theories.

Super-Higgs mechanism

Words: 42
Supergravity OurBigBook.com
When local supersymmetry is spontaneously broken, the gravitino absorbs the goldstino and becomes massive. The two goldstino states provide its longitudinal spin-1/2 polarizations. With only global supersymmetry breaking, the goldstino remains a physical massless particle. An ordinary supersymmetric Higgs mechanism instead makes an internal spin-one gauge boson massive and can leave supersymmetry unbroken.

Gravitino (ψμ​)

Words: 42
Supergravity OurBigBook.com
The gravitino is the spin-3/2 gauge field of local supersymmetry and the partner of the graviton. A massless four-dimensional gravitino has two physical helicities, ±3/2; a massive one has four, adding ±1/2. The super-Higgs mechanism supplies these extra states from the goldstino.

No-scale supergravity

Words: 628 Articles: 7
Supergravity OurBigBook.com
In a no-scale sector, the Kähler metric satisfies Ki​Kijˉ​Kjˉ​​=3. If the superpotential is independent of that sector, its covariant derivatives contribute 3eK∣W∣2, cancelling the universal −3eK∣W∣2 in the supergravity F-term potential. Spectator sectors can still contribute to the potential. This cancellation permits zero-energy minima with broken supersymmetry and exact flat scalar directions.

Matter-logarithm no-scale potential (V=eK(s2∣DS​W∣2+3t​∣WC​∣2))

Words: 336 Articles: 3
No-scale supergravity OurBigBook.com
For s=S+Sˉ>0, t=T+Tˉ−∣C∣2>0, K=−logs−3logt and a holomorphic superpotential independent of T, the exact F-term potential is V=eK[s2∣DS​W∣2+(t/3)∣WC​∣2]. Inverting the mixed T,C metric gives KTTˉ=t(t+∣C∣2)/3, KTCˉ=tCˉ/3, KCTˉ=tC/3, and KCCˉ=t/3. Substitution of DT​W=−3W/t and DC​W=WC​+3CˉW/t cancels all mixed terms, leaving 3∣W∣2+(t/3)∣WC​∣2; the first term cancels the supergravity negative term.
No-scale volume runaway criterion (V=A/y3+B/y2,∂y​V=−3A/y4−2B/y3)
Words: 79
Matter-logarithm no-scale potential OurBigBook.com
If a no-scale supergravity scalar potential has the displayed form with y>0 and nonnegative A,B independent of the volume coordinate y, every point with A+B>0 has a direction of strictly decreasing potential. Thus a finite stationary vacuum requires A=B=0. If that common zero set is empty, the potential has infimum zero along y→∞ but no finite minimum. If the common zero set is nonempty, varying y on it is a flat direction of a scalar potential. This distinguishes an attained zero-energy vacuum from a decompactification runaway.
Cubic-matter no-scale vacuum with an exponential dilaton (Vmin​=0,FT=0 on the nontrivial finite branch)
Words: 194 Articles: 1
Matter-logarithm no-scale potential OurBigBook.com
For W=C3+A+b, A=ae−αS, the potential is V=∣C3+b+(1+αs)A∣2/(st3)+3∣C∣4/(st2). A finite zero-energy vacuum requires C=0 and b+(1+αs)A=0. With a,b=0, such a solution exists exactly when 0<∣b/a∣≤2e−1/2: the magnitude equation is ∣b/a∣=(1+x)e−x/2, x=αs>0, whose maximum occurs at x=1. At that vacuum FS=FC=0 but FT=eK/2tWˉ=0. Both components of T are flat, while C is quartically lifted. If no root exists, the positive potential falls toward zero as t→∞ and has no finite minimum. If a=b=0, the C=0 family is supersymmetric instead.
Quartic stabilization at a double no-scale root (V∼(ReS−s0​)4)
Words: 101
Cubic-matter no-scale vacuum with an exponential dilaton OurBigBook.com
For the cubic-matter no-scale vacuum with an exponential dilaton, put x=S+Sˉ and A=ae−αS. At C=0, zero energy requires G(S)=b+(1+αx)A=0. On a fixed-imaginary-part slice, s=ReS gives dG/ds=α(1−2αs)A. At the double root s0​=1/(2α), the first derivative vanishes but the second is −2α2A, so G=−α2A(s−s0​)2+O((s−s0​)3). Therefore V=∣G∣2/(xy3) begins at fourth order. This real scalar has zero quadratic mass but is not an exact flat direction of a scalar potential. The imaginary part of S is still lifted quadratically, and the matter field C also has a quartic leading potential. Exact flat directions instead come from the complex volume modulus T along the zero-energy locus.

No-scale vacuum with a cubic matter superpotential (K=−3log(T+Tˉ)+∣C∣2,W=C3+B)

Words: 60
No-scale supergravity OurBigBook.com
The no-scale supergravity identity cancels the negative gravitino contribution, leaving V=e∣C∣2∣3C2+Cˉ(C3+B)∣2/(T+Tˉ)3. Zero-energy minima occur at C=0 and, for B=0, three phase-related nonzero solutions with ∣B∣=∣C∣(3+∣C∣2). Their T supergravity auxiliary field is nonzero if B=0, while both real components of T are flat on each vacuum branch. For B=0, the C=0 branch is instead supersymmetric and has zero gravitino mass from a superpotential.

Finite zero-energy vacuum for a single exponential superpotential

Words: 92
No-scale supergravity OurBigBook.com
For K=−log(S+Sˉ)−3log(T+Tˉ) and W=ae−αS+b with α>0, the potential is ∣b+[1+α(S+Sˉ)]ae−αS∣2/[(S+Sˉ)(T+Tˉ)3]. With nonzero a,b, a finite zero-energy vacuum exists exactly when 0<∣b/a∣≤2e−1/2. To prove this, set x=αReS>0; the magnitude equation is ∣b/a∣=(1+2x)e−x, whose derivative changes sign at x=1/2 and whose maximum is 2e−1/2. The phase fixes the imaginary part of S. At a zero-energy solution the T auxiliary field remains nonzero, so supersymmetry is broken and both real components of T are flat. If a=b=0, the family is instead supersymmetric.

Words: 90
No-scale supergravity OurBigBook.com
Let K=−3logΓ where Γ>0 is twice differentiable and homogeneous of degree one. If the Kähler Hessian is invertible, the Euler theorem for homogeneous functions identities give τi​Kij​=3Γj​/Γ, then Kij−1​Γj​/Γ=τi​/3 and Γi​Kij−1​Γj​/Γ2=1/3. Multiplication by nine gives the no-scale identity. A positive degree-one Γ need not induce an invertible or positive Kähler metric: Γ=τ1​+τ2​ gives a rank-one metric for K. The Hessian matrix (Γij​) itself always has the radial null vector τ, whereas the Hessian matrix of K can be invertible. In a larger theory the relevant full inverse metric, or a decoupled block, must obey the identity.

After eliminating the chiral auxiliary fields in Planck-unit supergravity, one convention gives Fi=−eK/2Kijˉ​Dj​W​. The upper-index inverse satisfies Kijˉ​​Kkjˉ​=δik​. Nonzero auxiliary expectation values diagnose supersymmetry breaking; their common phase convention does not affect the vanishing condition.

Supergravity OurBigBook.com
Four-dimensional N=8 supergravity has eight independent Weyl spinor supercharges. Its supergravity multiplet has helicities from 2 to −2, with multiplicities 1,8,28,56,70,56,28,8,1.

Supergravity OurBigBook.com
A supergravity multiplet is a supermultiplet containing a graviton and its supersymmetric partners. In four-dimensional N=8 supergravity, the irreducible massless supermultiplet contains 128 boson and 128 fermion states.

Supergravity moment-map constraint on D-term breaking (P=iκ−2kiDi​W/W(W=0))

Words: 94
Supergravity F-term potential OurBigBook.com
Let ki generate a holomorphic gauge transformation, with ki∂i​W=−κ2rW and moment map P=i(kiKi​−r). Substitution of the Kähler covariant derivative of a superpotential gives the displayed identity. Consequently, a finite point with W=0 and all Di​W=0 also has P=0. Pure D-term breaking with vanishing chiral auxiliary fields can therefore evade this argument only where W=0 or outside its hypotheses. In conventional two-derivative matter-coupled supergravity, a constant Fayet–Iliopoulos term gauges an R-symmetry and constrains the transformation of W; a neutral superpotential and an independently assigned nonzero constant shift are not generally consistent. The gauge-covariance restriction is derived in Van Proeyen's discussion of Fayet–Iliopoulos terms and R-symmetry.

The gravitino mass parameter in four-dimensional supergravity is the displayed expression. In a zero-energy supersymmetry breaking vacuum with only F-term breaking, Kijˉ​​FiFj=3m3/22​/κ2. Writing this norm as ΛSUSY4​ gives m3/2​=ΛSUSY2​/(3​mp​). It is small relative to ΛSUSY​ when the breaking scale is below the Planck mass. The super-Higgs mechanism supplies the longitudinal gravitino states.

The Kähler covariant derivative of a superpotential transforms by the same holomorphic factor as the superpotential under a Kähler transformation. This follows by differentiating e−fW and cancelling the extra derivative of f against the shift of Ki​.

The Polonyi model uses a canonical Kähler potential and a superpotential linear in one chiral superfield to obtain spontaneous supersymmetry breaking.

Words: 74
Polonyi model OurBigBook.com
For m=0 and positive β, the Polonyi model has a unique zero-energy global minimum at β=2−3​, ⟨z⟩=3​−1. Writing u=Rez−(3​−1) and y=Imz, its potential bracket is (u2+y2+3​u)2+(23​−3)u2+(4−23​)y2, a sum of nonnegative terms. The real and imaginary curvatures are 43​ and 8−43​. The other zero-energy stationary point with β=2+3​ and z=−3​−1 is a saddle point. The stable vacuum has nonzero supergravity auxiliary field, so it has supersymmetry breaking even with zero cosmological constant. The m=0 branch does not fix these values.
Polonyi supersymmetry branches (Dz​W=m2[1+zˉ(z+β)])
Words: 57
Polonyi model OurBigBook.com
For the Polonyi model with canonical Kähler potential and W=m2(z+β), β>0, a constant supersymmetric vacuum with m=0 requires real z=(−β±β2−4​)/2 and exists exactly for β≥2. Its supergravity F-term potential is negative because W=0. For 0<β<2, the supergravity auxiliary field cannot vanish. If m=0, the model is flat with unbroken supersymmetry. This parameter-dependent statement is sharper than asserting that every linear superpotential breaks supersymmetry in supergravity.

A spurion is a nondynamical background field assigned transformation properties so that couplings or symmetry-breaking parameters can be treated as if they arose from symmetry-covariant fields.
